doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Hall's arranging by ear and transposing
summary: Hall wrote arrangements from ear with no piano; Albert mentions Lloyd Glenn and Billy Douglas arranging from their heads.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you use arrangements with small groups?
Very seldom. Very seldom. Do you have arrangements? No. Do I have arrangements? Yeah.
Do you have arrangements with small groups? If you know the theme song, You Don't Love Me? The sex, I mean thought, I ran it.
With all the implied double-toning and all that. Right. Yes, I remember it, right? Right. Right. Yeah. Did you have a favorite arrangement here?
It just came out of your head? Yeah.
Did you have to work at a piano or a chord instrument of any kind?
Well, I knew nothing about the piano. Didn't have any piano. All this was from ear training. Yeah. So I wrote the melody down, then I stopped at the harmony, but I could hear it. No training.
You knew enough by ear though to know the harmony and how to make the variations. Right.
Right. And it's not straight melody.
Then Lloyd Glenn helped out some.
Oh, I see. With some part of your business.
I just wonder, because so many people arrange at the piano and... Most of them do.

Well, we had another one like all that didn't use the piano. He might know anything about the piano. It's for Billy Douglas to sound like the whole arrangement out of his head. He couldn't touch any history. What about the... Yeah, it is.
We can continue. Did you have any trouble with transposition or anything? No. I mean for the various instruments.
Oh, right. Because that would be in different keys. Yes. At first I had a little bit of power, but after I had this...
I see, because things do make a difference that way.
